name: Rust-backed stateless node memory and request capacity

description: Baseline concurrent mixed Rust codec workload and live worker memory

asi.hypothesis: Establish fixed mixed workload capacity proxy before changes
asi.observations: Repeated metric labels consume 512000 result words for 8000 samples; label rebuilding is largest retained-term opportunity. All non-integration tests and Rust tests pass.
asi.limitations: Local codec pipeline capacity proxy excludes HTTP networking and S3 latency. RSS high-water includes fixture creation.

description: Share consecutive identical metric label maps and matcher decisions within each Arrow batch

asi.hypothesis: Immutable labels maps can be shared across consecutive equal canonical bytes with a single-entry cache
asi.observations: Repeated metric retained words fell 512000 to 148002 and live worker MiB fell 6.36 to 2.43. Filtered live memory 0.36 to 0.14. Unique label memory unchanged. Cache uses full bytes, not hash, and stores negative matches too.
asi.caveat: Unmodified logs/JSON/write throughput also increased substantially, indicating baseline host contention or warmup noise. Need unchanged verification, do not attribute entire throughput gain to this change.
asi.validation: Full available tests pass; added hash-collision/same-caller-ID, empty-label transitions, all matcher ops, budget and actual heap sharing tests.

description: Unchanged verification confirms deterministic memory savings but severe throughput noise

asi.hypothesis: Verify kept optimization with identical source before proceeding
asi.rollback_reason: No code candidate in this verification; capacity below prior best, preserve already committed optimization.
asi.next_action_hint: Throughput fluctuates >2x across unchanged runs; inspect host load, use longer rounds and more robust paired controls. Memory metrics stable to the byte.
asi.observations: Retained sizes identical to run 2 for every workload, so 61.7% repeated-series live-memory reduction is reliable despite CPU noise.

name: Stateless codec capacity: longer mixed workload sampling

description: Reset baseline with tenfold longer throughput sampling to reduce contention noise

asi.hypothesis: Longer sampling reduces temporal noise without changing fixed payloads or algorithms
asi.observations: 480 operations per case per round now vs 48. Baseline includes kept single-entry labels sharing. Memory metrics same as before.
asi.limitations: Host load still fluctuates; demand repeated verification for tiny changes. Peak RSS depends on allocator high-water mark and accumulated runs.

description: Borrow Arrow canonical-label bytes and copy only accepted labels instead of an Erlang column arena

asi.hypothesis: Avoid copying entire label columns, especially for long strings and sparse queries, by allocating one accepted distinct label set
asi.rollback_reason: Primary capacity 596.55 vs 935.53; standard fixtures short labels yield identical retained memory. Peak RSS lower but confounded by contention.
asi.next_action_hint: Revisit only with paired measurement and legitimate long-label holdout; no need to modify fixed benchmark to favor it. Next try metric writer borrowed labels.
asi.observations: All tests pass including new long-label check showing only selected 1100-byte value retained, not entire arena. Existing make_subbinary already copies <=64-byte labels so baseline short-label live memory unaffected. Unmodified log/JSON rps fell by ~38% too, indicating host contention.
asi.implementation: Removed BinaryArena (and copied offsets), parse labels_arr.value(row), NewBinary copied per accepted distinct label key/value, kept one-entry map cache.

description: Borrow metric writer label key/value bytes directly, eliminating per-label HashMap allocations

asi.hypothesis: Borrow immutable BEAM label slices to remove two Vec allocations per label plus HashMap hashing per sample
asi.rollback_reason: Mixed primary score 637 vs 935 baseline, though changed writer rps improved slightly while unmodified cases slowed 25-49%. Retained BEAM memory unaffected.
asi.next_action_hint: Need paired reference control under highly variable host load before throughput-only writer optimizations; next try deterministic log resource sharing.
asi.observations: Compiles safely using Binary<'a> as_slice lifetime, all tests pass. Writer 426 vs 417 rps with other paths lower suggests real benefit masked by contention, promising retry when paired controls available.
asi.implementation: Remove HashMap import; MapIterator collects borrowed (&[u8], &[u8]) pairs, sorts by key, finds __name__ in pairs.

description: Share consecutive equal log resource maps within Arrow batches

asi.hypothesis: Share immutable repeated resource metadata on logs without caching high-cardinality records
asi.rollback_reason: Primary score below baseline under severe host contention despite clear memory reduction; obey keep/discard contract.
asi.next_action_hint: Switch to paired frozen-reference benchmark before any further code trials. This is a promising retry after measurement assumptions change.
asi.observations: Log live memory 1.79 -> 1.22 MiB (-32%); result words 164288 -> 122540. Unmodified metric filtered rps simultaneously -71%, so absolute comparisons unreliable. All correctness tests pass.
asi.implementation: One-entry previous_resource Option<(&[u8],Term)> in materialize; compare full raw JSON bytes, null/empty use empty_map; tests assert :erts_debug.same and resource transitions/time filtering.

name: Paired frozen-reference Rust codec capacity per live MiB

description: Paired frozen-reference baseline with alternating ordering and output equality checks

asi.hypothesis: Pair candidate with same-process frozen reference to control host CPU variation
asi.observations: Identical code yields 0.960 index, ~4% noise/bias remains rather than 30–60% absolute swings. Memory sizes exactly equal. Frozen reference revision 8876777 includes kept metric-label map sharing.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry log resource sharing from run 7 under paired controls, then writer borrowing from run 6.

description: Retry log resource-map sharing under paired controls: 32% less live log memory

asi.hypothesis: Log resource metadata repeats in service-sorted runs, so share immutable maps after full JSON byte equality
asi.changed_assumption: Frozen same-process paired controls replace unreliable absolute throughput comparisons under host contention.
asi.observations: Log paired throughput ratio 1.0609 and memory ratio 1.4703; capacity contribution 1.56x. Mixed paired index 1.089 vs 0.960 baseline. Log memory reduction deterministic at 32%. Single-entry cache stays bounded for unique resources.
asi.validation: All correctness tests pass plus resource transition/time filtering/actual heap sharing test; candidate/reference output equality verified on all six workloads.

description: Retry borrowed metric writer label bytes with paired controls: 1.54x writer throughput

asi.hypothesis: Replace per-sample owned label HashMap with sorted borrowed binary slices to eliminate allocations and hashing
asi.changed_assumption: Same-process paired frozen reference now isolates speed difference from whole-host CPU swings.
asi.observations: Writer paired throughput 1.5398x; mixed index rises 1.089 -> 1.155. Retained memory same (writer benefit is transient native allocations). Absolute throughput again collapsed under host contention but paired measurement survives.
asi.validation: Full existing ExUnit/Rust tests and baseline output equality pass. No unsafe lifetimes: borrowed slices are only held during NIF env lifetime; returned Row stores owned derived fields.

description: Retry selective metric label copies under paired controls; unique/repeated read throughput regresses

asi.hypothesis: Parse borrowed Arrow canonical labels and copy accepted distinct labels, removing whole-column Erlang arena
asi.changed_assumption: Paired controls remove absolute throughput contention confounding; previous kept writer/log optimizations retained.
asi.rollback_reason: Mixed primary 1.1247 < 1.1549 best; paired repeated/unique reads 0.826/0.882x reference, while standard short-label retained memory unchanged.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not retry unconditional per-label copies again. A hybrid arena for short labels with copy-on-retain for long labels could bound long-label pinning without sacrificing small-label performance.
asi.observations: Long-label isolation correctness test passes, but per-key NewBinary allocations can cost more than subbinary materialization. Filtered case 1.107x faster; broad read workloads matter too.

description: Share derived metric writer label metadata across equal-map runs and drop rows before compression

asi.hypothesis: Consecutive equivalent Erlang label maps can reuse canonical bytes, JSON and stable hash; Rc shares metadata through stable row sorting
asi.observations: Writer paired ratio 3.120x frozen reference (was 1.54x with just borrowed slices); mixed index 1.244 >1.155. Row holds one Rc instead of three owned Vecs. Drop rows and one-entry cache after Arrow batch built to reduce compression-time peak native memory.
asi.correctness: Full map equality, not IDs, bounds cache lookup to one entry; unique labels get normal extraction. Tests cover Unicode/escaped strings, equal labels with varying explicit/nil IDs, empty-map transitions and invalid label key/value rejection. All ExUnit/Rust tests and reference output equality pass.
asi.next_action_hint: Run high-cardinality/long-label writer holdout before trusting 3x across all ingest shapes. Consider column capacities and JSON map allocation next.

description: Verify kept codecs on unique/shuffled/long-label writer holdouts and real loopback MCP HTTP

asi.hypothesis: Confirm writer optimizations generalize beyond repeated labels and assess HTTP end-to-end transfer
asi.observations: Frozen-reference writer holdouts: unique1.232x, long repeated labels3.892x, shuffled1.184x. Codec capacity unchanged source index varies1.244->1.337; noise remains. HTTP metrics1.052x, logs0.920x means HTTP gains not convincingly established.
asi.http_limitations: Single-concurrency actual Req->Bandit->Phoenix->MCP request, unchanged admission controls, 2000 records returned and validated; frozen decoder differs only at read NIF, common candidate HTTP/JSON code. Local immutable Parquet fixture replaces S3 I/O. Not production capacity or saturation.
asi.next_action_hint: HTTP encodes large escaped inner JSON text; general JSON encoding may dominate and bottleneck overall requests. Optimize response serialization without protocol changes.

description: Portable word-at-a-time JSON escape scanning; Rust test method ambiguity prevents keep

asi.hypothesis: Scan unescaped JSON strings eight bytes at a time using conservative SWAR detection without unsafe code
asi.rollback_reason: Rust test compilation fails: input.extend(array) ambiguous between Extend and out::Sink. ExUnit passed. Mixed metric slightly below best anyway.
asi.next_action_hint: Fix tests with extend_from_slice(&array) if revisiting; avoid per-eight-byte overhead for short/dense-escape strings. JSON paired throughput0.952x suggests no broad win.
asi.error: E0034 json_write.rs test line121. Not algorithm semantic failure.
asi.unmeasured_metrics: All holdout metrics use sentinel0 because holdout was not run this iteration; tool requires every secondary. Do not interpret as real zeros. Future iterations must run measure+holdout.

description: Avoid JSON binary-key entry vectors; unrelated query-slot cleanup assertion fails under load

asi.hypothesis: Avoid intermediate Vec allocations for JSON binary-key maps with two MapIterator passes; mixed keys retain full collision checks
asi.rollback_reason: ExUnit admission test checks Registry slot cleanup too early under load, leaving one worker PID visible; cannot keep failed checks. Primary1.3389 only0.15% above best, within noise.
asi.next_action_hint: Inspect query-slot test synchronization without weakening admission assertions. Binary-key map encoder gain not proven; prioritize memory changes instead.
asi.failure: test/pulso/promql/evaluator_test.exs:77 expected Registry.lookup(QuerySlots,{acme,0}) == [] but one PID remained. Existing 605 other tests pass.
asi.implementation: MapIterator all key.get_type==Binary then stream direct to Sink, else existing Vec path. No semantic mismatches.

name: Paired Rust request capacity including MCP metric response serialization

description: Add real MCP metric response serialization workload before optimizing output copies; synchronize flaky worker-exit test

asi.hypothesis: End-to-end metric response encoding deserves measurement alongside decoder-only tests; baseline added before candidate output changes
asi.observations: Read+JSON response baseline377.65 rps,2.9048MiB versus read-only900.75rps2.43MiB. Seven-case paired baseline1.2956. Existing optimizations preserved.
asi.test_fix: Monitor actual blocked query workers before release, wait for all DOWNs after results, then retain original slot assertions. Full checks pass, avoids result-before-worker-exit race without sleeps.
asi.limitations: HTTP holdout contrasts only decoder NIF because common current encoder used on both paths; future encoder gain needs separate frozen response encoding validation.

description: Write metric JSON directly into Erlang BinSink instead of Vec plus final copy

asi.hypothesis: Eliminate final metric JSON memcpy by writing to growable Erlang-owned output
asi.rollback_reason: Primary1.2455 below1.2956 baseline; read+response paired0.9429x reference, live memory unchanged. Saving copy does not offset growable binary writer overhead here.
asi.next_action_hint: Cache and repeat serialized labels by full Term equality before reconsidering direct Erlang output; maybe better capacity estimates later. Do not assume fewer copies always faster.
asi.observations: All checks pass including new randomized native response parity, large-growth/trailing-byte correctness, empty/unsupported input tests. Existing scalar writer semantics unchanged.
asi.implementation: metric_json encode returns Binary via BinSink; helpers generic Sink, lib.rs passes resulting binary through rather than copy. Test file added but discarded with candidate.

description: Reuse serialized label JSON ranges for consecutive equivalent metric label maps

asi.hypothesis: Single-entry full-map equality cache reuses prior label JSON output via Vec.extend_from_within, avoiding repeated native decoding and escaping
asi.observations: Read+response paired ratio1.183x vs reference; mixed1.3149 vs1.2956 baseline, ~1.5% total gain. Existing writer ratio also fluctuated upward, so verify unchanged before trusting mixed improvement magnitude.
asi.correctness: New metric_json_test randomized reference parity includes empty/repeated/unique labels, varying IDs, Unicode/control escapes, large output reallocations, integer/nil samples and invalid fields. Full ExUnit/Rust tests pass.
asi.next_action_hint: Verify, then consider direct Erlang BinSink again only with changed assumptions (serialized-label work removed); Vec copy might not be bottleneck.

description: Unchanged verification: metric JSON label reuse benefit persists, mixed paired score still noisy

asi.hypothesis: Verify kept serialized metric labels reuse without source changes
asi.rollback_reason: Verification score below best; no code candidate to roll back, keep already committed implementation.
asi.observations: Response paired1.110x vs1.183x prior, so path-local benefit reproduced; mixed score varies6%. Writer paired2.675x vs3.761x prior. Deterministic memory savings persist.
asi.next_action_hint: Memory-focused log string/attribute term reuse could make larger robust gains. Add response holdout on unique labels to avoid assuming repeated-label advantage universally.
